raw_response:
## Recommended starting point: PlantUML Salt

[PlantUML Salt](https://plantuml.com/salt) is the closest match I found to the workflow you describe: write a short textual specification of a UI and have a renderer lay out the wireframe. Its official documentation shows buttons, input fields, checkboxes, radio buttons and dropdowns, with braces and pipes for arranging controls into a grid. That makes it a strong first option for the same kind of convenience you associate with Mermaid.

For example, this small form follows its documented syntax:

```text
@startsalt
{+
  Email | "                 "
  Secret | "                 "
  [Back] | [Continue]
}
@endsalt
```

The recommendation concerns Salt's wireframing language; it does not require Mermaid compatibility. The syntax and controls are documented, but I have not run this example or measured authoring speed. [Official Salt syntax](https://plantuml.com/salt).

## Alternatives worth comparing

| Tool | Authoring approach | Why it may fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [wiremark](https://wiremark.dev/) | Indented component names such as Stack, TextField and Button | A compact structural language with a browser editor; sources can be standalone files or embedded Markdown blocks through the appropriate host adapters. |
| [wiremd](https://github.com/akonan/wiremd/) | Markdown plus UI and layout extensions | A useful choice if Markdown already feels natural. Its README documents rendering to HTML and a CLI watch mode with live reload. |
| [WireDSL](https://github.com/Wire-DSL/wire-dsl) | Explicit declarations of projects, screens, layouts and components | A more structured alternative with a browser editor, live SVG preview and documented SVG, PNG and PDF exports. |

For the shortest route to evaluating the idea, start with Salt and compare its notation with wiremark's indentation-based syntax. Try wiremd if familiar Markdown is your main preference; consider WireDSL if explicit screen and layout declarations suit the designs you want to express. This ordering is a judgment about fit to your concise-authoring goal, not a benchmark.

All four have primary documentation supporting the core requirement: authoring wireframes through text. I have not imposed an operating-system, license, price, export-format or integration requirement because the question does not supply one. In particular, comparing the effort of writing HTML does not prohibit a tool that produces HTML from a shorter source language.

These are documentation-based recommendations, not installation or usability tests. The evidence is live and undated, so I cannot establish from these pages that every described feature was available on 7 November 2026. A search snippet reports a later wiremark repository update; it does not establish the project's original release date.
